strategy: Build distinct, source-verified pages around the Dopamine 3 ecosystem. Never create near-duplicate firmware pages when one compatibility page can satisfy the same intent.
common_facts: The official Dopamine 3.x README describes Dopamine as a rootless semi-untethered jailbreak.
The official Dopamine 3.x README lists iOS 15.0 through 17.3.1 for arm64e.
The official Dopamine 3.x README separately lists iOS 15.0 through 18.7.1 plus iOS 26.0 through 26.0.1 for A12 and A13 devices.
The official Dopamine 3.x README lists iOS 15.0 through 18.7.1 for arm64.
The shorthand labels iOS 15 and iOS 16 may be used only inside the documented continuous ranges and must preserve the architecture or chip-family limits.
The shorthand label iOS 17 may be used only with the exact documented architecture or chip limits and must not imply point releases beyond the cited endpoint.
The shorthand label iOS 18 may be used only for categories whose documented range reaches iOS 18.7.1 and must not imply universal support across every device.
The shorthand label iOS 26 may be used only for A12 and A13 and must not imply versions beyond the explicitly documented iOS 26.0 through 26.0.1 range.
Within the documented continuous iOS 15.0 through 18.7.1 range for A12/A13 and arm64, iOS 16.0, iOS 17.0 and iOS 18.0 are inside that range; arm64e has its separate endpoint at iOS 17.3.1.
The Dopamine 3.x README points to https://ellekit.space/dopamine/ as the official website and download location.

The official Dopamine website describes Dopamine as rootless and identifies Sileo and Zebra as package managers associated with Dopamine; its displayed compatibility text may lag the newer 3.x README, so the 3.x README is the authority for current version ranges.
The official Dopamine website explains that rootless jailbreaks only allow writes to certain parts of the filesystem and that tweaks may need to be updated or recompiled for rootless support.
The existing Next Jailbreak Dopamine 3 iOS 17.6.1 guide is at dopamine-3-jailbreak-ios-17-6-1.html and includes a real Next Jailbreak test-device visual.

existing_pages.intent: Dopamine 3 jailbreak guide for iOS/iPadOS 17.6.1 on supported A12-family and A13 devices

topics.intent: Complete Dopamine 3 compatibility hub covering arm64e iOS 15.0–17.3.1, A12/A13 iOS 15.0–18.7.1 plus the separate iOS 26.0–26.0.1 range, and arm64 iOS 15.0–18.7.1
facts: This page is the central compatibility hub and must distinguish the three official compatibility lines instead of collapsing them into one range.

The complete compatibility summary for the hub is: arm64e is documented from iOS 15.0 through iOS 17.3.1; A12 and A13 are documented from iOS 15.0 through iOS 18.7.1 plus a separate iOS 26.0 through iOS 26.0.1 range; arm64 is documented from iOS 15.0 through iOS 18.7.1.
Whenever the hub summarizes A12/A13 support, it must mention the additional separate iOS 26.0 through iOS 26.0.1 range and must not describe iOS 18.7.1 as the final A12/A13 endpoint.

The A12/A13 ranges are separate: the source does not state that versions after iOS 18.7.1 and before iOS 26.0 are supported. Do not turn the two documented ranges into one continuous iOS 15.0 through iOS 26.0.1 claim.
For current version ranges, use the 3.x README facts in common_facts rather than the older compatibility text still visible on the official website.
Link readers to narrower guides instead of duplicating every installation tutorial on the hub page.

topics.intent: Dopamine 3 iOS 26.0 and 26.0.1 jailbreak compatibility for A12 and A13
facts: The Dopamine 3.x README explicitly lists iOS 26.0 through 26.0.1 for A12 and A13 devices.
The same README does not state iOS 26 support for the general arm64e range or for arm64; do not extend the iOS 26 claim beyond A12 and A13.

topics.intent: Dopamine 3 iOS 18 compatibility for A12 and A13 devices
facts: The Dopamine 3.x README lists A12 and A13 support through iOS 18.7.1 before the separate iOS 26.0 through 26.0.1 range.
The general arm64e range in the same README stops at iOS 17.3.1, so this page must not imply that all arm64e devices share the A12/A13 iOS 18 range.

topics.intent: What DarkSword is and how it relates to Dopamine jailbreak development
facts: opa334 describes darksword-kexploit as an iOS <=26.0.1 DarkSword kernel exploit reimplemented in Objective-C.
An official Dopamine 2.5 beta release note added the DarkSword kernel exploit as an option, establishing a documented relationship between DarkSword and Dopamine development.
Do not claim that historical beta limitations or known issues still apply to the current Dopamine 3.x branch unless a current official source explicitly confirms them.

topics.intent: Sileo and Dopamine 3: package manager role, repositories and rootless package checks
facts: The official Sileo repository describes Sileo as a modern APT package manager frontend and its repository description says it is a modern package manager for iOS 11 and higher.
The official Dopamine website identifies Sileo and Zebra as package managers associated with Dopamine.
The official Dopamine website advises users to check that tweaks are compatible and properly compiled for the rootless environment rather than assuming every tweak works out of the box.

topics.intent: Dopamine 3 vs Dopamine 2 compatibility ranges and what changed at a high level
facts: The Dopamine 2.x README describes Dopamine as a rootless semi-untethered jailbreak for iOS 15.0 through 16.5.1 on arm64e and iOS 15.0 through 15.8.6 / 16.0 through 16.6.1 on arm64.
The Dopamine 3.x README expands the documented ranges to iOS 15.0 through 17.3.1 for arm64e, iOS 15.0 through 18.7.1 plus 26.0 through 26.0.1 for A12/A13, and iOS 15.0 through 18.7.1 for arm64.
Do not invent feature differences beyond these documented compatibility and project-description facts.

topics.intent: Dopamine 3 vs TrollStore: jailbreak versus permanent IPA installation and supported versions
facts: The official TrollStore README describes TrollStore as a permasigned jailed app that can permanently install IPAs opened in it.
The TrollStore README lists supported versions as 14.0 beta 2 through 16.6.1, 16.7 RC (20H18), and 17.0.
The TrollStore README states that 16.7.x other than 16.7 RC and 17.0.1+ will never be supported unless another CoreTrust bug is discovered.
The Dopamine 3.x README describes Dopamine as a rootless semi-untethered jailbreak with the current version ranges provided in common_facts.
TrollStore and Dopamine therefore serve different primary purposes; do not describe TrollStore itself as a jailbreak.

topics.intent: What rootless means in Dopamine 3 and why tweak compatibility must be checked
facts: The official Dopamine website says rootless jailbreaks do not provide full access to the operating system because only certain parts of the filesystem can be written to.
The same official page says modifications may need to be done differently and tweaks may need updates to properly support rootless.
The official page advises users to check tweak compatibility and whether tweaks are properly compiled before installing them.

topics.intent: Dopamine 3 arm64 support range for older A8 through A11 class devices
facts: The Dopamine 3.x README lists iOS 15.0 through 18.7.1 for arm64.
The official Dopamine website identifies arm64 with A8 through A11 in its architecture explanation, although its displayed firmware compatibility text is older than the 3.x README.
Use the current 3.x README for the firmware range and the official website only for the arm64 A8-through-A11 architecture explanation.

topics.intent: Where to get Dopamine 3 from the official project and how to avoid confusing unofficial download pages
facts: The Dopamine 3.x README explicitly points to https://ellekit.space/dopamine/ as the official website and download location.
The project itself is open source on the opa334/Dopamine GitHub repository.
This article must direct readers to the verified official project pages and must not mirror, rehost, or invent a binary download link.

topics.intent: Best source-verified tweaks for Dopamine 3 and modern rootless jailbreaks
facts: Requires dynamic verified package metadata before unattended publication.
rules: Only include packages whose current verified metadata supports the relevant architecture/environment.
Update the existing page instead of creating monthly near-duplicates.

topics.intent: How to safely update Dopamine 3 when a new official release is published
facts: Requires current release-specific update instructions before unattended publication.
rules: Refresh this URL for new versions rather than publishing one page per point release.

topics.intent: Dopamine 3 common jailbreak failures and source-backed troubleshooting
facts: Requires current source-backed issue and fix data before unattended publication.
rules: Only include a failure or fix when it is documented by the official project, release notes, or a maintainer response.
Do not generalize one user's issue into a universal fix.
